data.question: Is Williamson's reported no-immediate-prison disposition materially more lenient than relevant Franklin County robbery sentencing comparators?
data.method: Compare the reported Williamson disposition against Ohio's F2 prison presumption and located Franklin County serial/bank-robbery cases, while coding material aggravating and mitigating differences.
data.scope: Franklin County robbery sentencing; comparator set is illustrative, not a population-level statistical sample.
findings: Williamson pleaded guilty to nine robbery counts, including five F2 counts.
Current reporting says he received no immediate prison.
Ohio law begins with a prison presumption for F2 felonies, subject to statutory findings.
Located Franklin County comparators produced 51 years (Gilbert), 13 years (Jarrett), and 24 years (Cunningham), while each comparator also contains material aggravating differences.
conclusions: A descriptive sentencing disparity is supported by the currently located evidence.
The evidence does not establish why the disparity occurred and does not prove athlete, political, racial, or other favoritism.
recommendations: Capture the Franklin County sentencing judgment and transcript.
Expand the comparator cohort and code plea/trial posture, prior record, weapon specification, number and degree of counts, restitution, mental-health mitigation, and post-arrest compliance.
counterarguments: The comparator cases are not identical; Gilbert and Cunningham contain aggravating factors, and Jarrett includes an aggravated-robbery firearm specification.
Community-control eligibility can turn on individualized statutory findings and mitigation not visible in news reporting.
limitations: The exact August 2026 Williamson sentencing entry and transcript have not yet been captured.
The comparator set is small and non-random.
unresolved: Exact R.C. 2929.13(D)(2) findings used by the sentencing court.
Exact community-control conditions, reserve term, restitution, and violation consequences.

title: Franklin County sentencing disparity analysis — Marcus Williamson
